title: Time-Based Key-Value Store
prompt: Design a time-based key-value store — think a versioned config or model-registry store. `set(key, value, timestamp)` stores the value at that timestamp. `get(key, timestamp)` returns the value set at the largest recorded timestamp <= the given timestamp, or an empty string if none exists.
constraints: Timestamps passed to set() for the same key are strictly increasing

test_cases.expected: see prompt — sequence of set/get calls, not a single call

hints: Store, per key, a list of (timestamp, value) pairs — since timestamps are strictly increasing per key, this list is already sorted.
get() then becomes a binary search for the largest timestamp <= the query timestamp within that key's list.
Python's bisect module (bisect_right on the timestamps) gets you this in O(log n) without hand-rolling binary search.
